{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**Prepared for:** Customer (internal)  
**Scope:** Verified playbook review of the Vendor-form Master Services Agreement. 19 rules assessed; 12 compliant, 6 deviations, 1 missing.

---

## 1. Executive summary

The risk-allocation core of this agreement is strong and does not require redlining. Indemnification (§ 20), limitation of liability (§ 21), IP and data ownership (§ 14, § 15.1), licence scope (§ 13), assignment and change of control (§ 24), warranties (§ 19), transition assistance and data return (§ 11), insurance (§ 18) and governing law/venue (§ 28) all meet our preferred positions, several of them exceeding it (hosted Services warranty runs for the full subscription term; indemnities sit outside the liability cap as Excluded Claims; § 12.3 affirmatively preserves our commercial freedom).

The problems are concentrated in a cluster of customer-side commitments and vendor-side control rights that are inconsistent with the rest of the document. Seven items require action:

- **Exclusivity (§ 2.2)** makes Vendor our sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services for the entire term, with no category limit, duration limit or performance exit. This is walk-away territory and contradicts both § 2.1 (no purchase commitment) and § 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges no exclusivity commitment). The same clause independently breaches the minimum-commitment rule by locking 100% of our demand.
- **Liquidated damages (§ 7.6)** impose USD 25,000 per day on us for any dependency delay — one-way, uncapped, with no materiality threshold or grace period, and apparently outside the § 21 liability regime.
- **No-solicitation (§ 12.4)** is one-sided, is an effective no-hire ("engage"), covers anyone employed by Vendor at any time, runs eighteen months post-termination and has no advertising carve-out.
- **No termination for convenience** anywhere in the document, against a three-year committed term under § 8.1.
- **Audit (§ 22.1)** permits unlimited unannounced audits with remote access to our systems, in direct conflict with the more reasonable §§ 22.2–22.3.
- **MFN (§ 7.2)** obliges us to extend Vendor the best terms we give any technology supplier, open-ended, and contradicts § 12.3.
- **Renewal (§ 8.2)** requires 180 days' non-renewal notice — double the 90-day walk-away threshold. Renewal pricing (§ 8.3) is already acceptable.

Several of these deviations are internally inconsistent with § 12.3, which records that we have made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. That inconsistency supports treating §§ 2.2, 7.2 and 12.4 as drafting overreach rather than a negotiated bargain.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Deviation | § 2.2 |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 7.6 |
| High | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § 9 (Termination) |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 22.1 |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments / volume restrictions | Deviation | § 2.2 |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Deviation | § 8.2 |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20.1 (Section 20 generally) |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14.1 (§§ 13.2, 14.2–14.4, 15.1) |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1 (Section 21 generally) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (Section 24 generally) |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 (§§ 13.2–13.4, 14.3) |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28.1 (§§ 28.2–28.3) |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11.1 (§§ 11.2–11.3) |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.2 (Section 19 generally) |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (§ 18.2) |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature, not trade material:

1. **§ 2.2 — full-term sole-supplier exclusivity.** No category limit, no duration limit, no performance-based exit. Our position: Vendor is a non-exclusive provider and we remain free to source from third parties. This single edit also resolves the MINCOMMIT deviation.
2. **§ 7.6 — USD 25,000/day Customer-payable liquidated damages.** One-way, uncapped, no materiality threshold or grace period, triggered by even brief delays, and not contained by §§ 21.2–21.3. Our position: replace with day-for-day schedule relief for Vendor, which addresses the delay risk without a Customer-payable penalty. The 3-month fallback is unavailable because this is not an early-termination fee.
3. **§ 12.4 — effective no-hire.** The "engage" prohibition is walk-away territory; the clause also fails the fallback on mutuality, personnel scope, duration and carve-outs. Fallback we will offer: mutual, personnel directly involved in the Services only, 12 months from the end of their involvement, no no-hire, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.
4. **Absence of any termination-for-convenience right** against the three-year term in § 8.1. Section 9 offers only for-cause exits, and §§ 8, 10, 11 and 27.3 add only non-renewal and force majeure. Our position: insert a 30-day convenience right with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, confirming Vendor has none (Vendor has no such right today, so this is confirmatory).
5. **§ 22.1 — unlimited unannounced audits with remote system access.** Fails the fallback on frequency, notice and system access, and conflicts with §§ 22.2–22.3. Our position: once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, off-site where practicable, no remote or direct system access.
6. **§ 7.2 — open-ended Customer-side MFN.** No product limitation, no 12-month cap, no comparison carve-outs. Our position: delete. No Vendor-granted MFN exists, so deletion costs us nothing.
7. **§ 8.2 — 180-day non-renewal notice.** Double the 90-day walk-away threshold and triple the 60-day fallback. Our position: 30-day opt-out with a Vendor renewal reminder. Renewal pricing under § 8.3 (lesser of CPI and 3%, 90 days' notice, no increase on prepaid periods) is acceptable and should be left alone.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the seven action items above, with the § 2.2 edit drafted once so it resolves both the exclusivity and minimum-commitment deviations. We should not raise the same commercial term twice with Vendor.
2. **Frame §§ 2.2, 7.2 and 12.4 as internal inconsistencies** with § 12.3, in which Vendor already acknowledges that we have made no exclusivity, MFC or no-hire commitment. This is our strongest and least contentious argument for removal.
3. **Hold §§ 2.2 and 7.6 as gating items.** We should not sign with full-term exclusivity or an uncapped daily penalty against us; if Vendor resists, escalate rather than trade.
4. **Where a fallback exists, lead with it** on § 12.4 (mutual, involved personnel, 12 months) and § 22.1 (annual audit on notice, no system access) to close quickly.
5. **Do not reopen the compliant sections.** Sections 11, 13, 14, 18, 19, 20, 21, 24 and 28 are at or above our preferred positions, and § 12.3 is affirmatively favourable to us — any Vendor attempt to reciprocate concessions from those provisions should be declined.
6. **Confirm the commercial owner accepts** the three-year term in § 8.1 on the assumption the 30-day convenience right is secured; if the convenience right is refused, the term length itself needs to be renegotiated."}
